summary_md: **Aleksandr Davydenko ([@Kotuke](https://x.com/Kotuke/status/2116083771921358937))** ships **Lumilo 0.2.0**, a macOS menu-bar panel that runs TensorFold (or Splash/llama.cpp), picks a model with its DFlash2 drafter, shows live tok/s and launches Claude Code or Codex against it, reporting Qwen3.8-27B at about 173 tok/s for code on an M5 Max; follow-ups note streamed numbers of ~150–170 tok/s for code, ~85 for English, ~37 for Russian, 43% draft acceptance, and that it is free, MIT and unofficial ([kotuke/lumilo](https://github.com/kotuke/lumilo)).

referenced_urls.title: GitHub - kotuke/lumilo: Menu-bar panel for local LLM engines on macOS: run Splash or llama.cpp, watch memory and speed, get models from Hugging Face

relevance: Speculative-decoding speeds for a ~27B local model wired to coding agents.
